[[File:Overfull graph.svg|thumb|This graph is '''overfull''' because its [[Graph (discrete mathematics)#Graph|size]] is larger than the product of its maximum [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] and the number of vertices in the graph (its [[Graph (discrete mathematics)#Graph|order]]) divided by 2 and rounded down. In this case, 22 <math>></math> 20.]]{{unsolved|mathematics|'''Conjecture:''' A graph ''G'' with <math>\Delta (G) > n/3</math> is class 2 [[if and only if]] it has an overfull subgraph S such that <math>\displaystyle \Delta (G) = \Delta (S)</math>.}}

In [[graph theory]], an '''overfull graph''' is a [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] whose [[Graph (discrete mathematics)#Graph|size]] is greater than the product of its maximum [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] and half of its [[Graph (discrete mathematics)#Graph|order]] [[floor and ceiling functions|floor]]ed, i.e. <math>|E| > \Delta (G) \lfloor |V|/2 \rfloor</math> where <math>|E|</math> is the size of ''G'', <math>\displaystyle\Delta(G)</math> is the maximum degree of ''G'', and <math>|V|</math> is the order of ''G''. The concept of an '''overfull subgraph''', an overfull graph that is a [[Glossary of graph theory#Subgraph|subgraph]], immediately follows. An alternate, stricter definition of an overfull subgraph ''S'' of a graph ''G'' requires <math>\displaystyle\Delta (G) = \Delta (S)</math>.

==Examples==
Every [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[cycle graph]] of length three or more is overfull. The product of its degree (two) and half its length (rounded down) is one less than the number of edges in the cycle. More generally, every [[regular graph]] with an odd number <math>n</math> of vertices is overfull, because its number of edges, <math>\Delta n/2</math> (where <math>\Delta</math> is its degree), is larger than <math>\Delta\lfloor n/2\rfloor</math>.

==Properties==
A few properties of overfull graphs:
# Overfull graphs are of odd order.
# Overfull graphs are [[Edge coloring#Properties|class 2]]. That is, they require at least {{math|&Delta; + 1}} colors in any [[edge coloring]].
# A graph ''G'', with an overfull subgraph ''S'' such that <math>\displaystyle\Delta (G) = \Delta (S)</math>, is of class 2.

==Overfull conjecture==
In 1986, [[Amanda Chetwynd]] and [[Anthony Hilton]] posited the following [[conjecture]] that is now known as the '''overfull conjecture'''.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Chetwynd | first1 = A. G.
 | last2 = Hilton | first2 = A. J. W.
 | doi = 10.1017/S030500410006610X
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
 | mr = 848854
 | pages = 303–317
 | title = Star multigraphs with three vertices of maximum degree
 | volume = 100
 | year = 1986| bibcode = 1986MPCPS.100..303C
 | url = https://eprints.lancs.ac.uk/id/eprint/19968/1/download2.pdf
 }}.</ref>

:A graph ''G'' with <math>\Delta (G) > n/3</math> is class 2 [[if and only if]] it has an overfull subgraph S such that <math>\displaystyle \Delta (G) = \Delta (S)</math>.

This conjecture, if true, would have numerous implications in graph theory, including the [[1-factorization conjecture]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Chetwynd | first1 = A. G.
 | last2 = Hilton | first2 = A. J. W.
 | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(89)90082-4
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | mr = 1001390
 | pages = 103–112
 | title = 1-factorizing regular graphs of high degree—an improved bound
 | volume = 75
 | year = 1989| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

==Algorithms==
For graphs in which <math>\Delta \ge n/3</math>, there are at most three [[induced subgraph|induced]] overfull subgraphs, and it is possible to find an overfull subgraph in [[polynomial time]]. When <math>\Delta \ge n/2</math>, there is at most one induced overfull subgraph, and it is possible to find it in [[linear time]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Niessen | first = Thomas
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Electronic Journal of Combinatorics
 | mr = 1814514
 | at = Research Paper 7
 | title = How to find overfull subgraphs in graphs with large maximum degree. II
 | url = http://www.combinatorics.org/Volume_8/Abstracts/v8i1r7.html
 | volume = 8
 | year = 2001}}.</ref>
